prompt: Leo has 12 apples 🍎. He shares them equally with 3 friends. How many apples does each friend get?
whyCorrect: 12 shared equally among 3 friends gives 4 apples each. 3 × 4 = 12!

whyWrongByChoice.a: If each got 3, that would be 3 × 3 = 9 apples. We have 12 to share.
whyWrongByChoice.c: If each got 5, that would need 3 × 5 = 15 apples. We only have 12.
whyWrongByChoice.d: If each got 6, that would need 3 × 6 = 18 apples. We only have 12.

conceptExplainer: Division is fair sharing. Distribute items into equal groups until all are shared.

miniLesson.title: Why Fair Sharing Works
bodyLines: When we share 12 things equally among 3 groups, each group gets 4.
You can check by multiplying backward: 3 groups × 4 apples = 12 total!

prompt: Leo wants to buy a notebook for $1.65. Which group of money makes exactly $1.65?
whyCorrect: 1 dollar ($1.00) + 2 quarters ($0.50) + 1 dime ($0.10) + 1 nickel ($0.05) equals exactly $1.65!

whyWrongByChoice.b: 1 dollar and 3 quarters is $1.00 + $0.75 = $1.75. That is 10 cents too much.
whyWrongByChoice.c: 1 dollar, 1 quarter, and 2 dimes is $1.00 + $0.25 + $0.20 = $1.45. That is 20 cents short.
whyWrongByChoice.d: 2 dollars is $2.00. That is more than the price.

conceptExplainer: Quarters are 25¢, dimes are 10¢, and nickels are 5¢. Add coins step by step.

whyCorrect: 8 + 5 is 13. Count on five from eight: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13.

whyWrongByChoice.a: 12 is 8 + 4. We need one more than that.
whyWrongByChoice.c: 14 is 8 + 6. That is one too many.

conceptExplainer: Adding joins two groups. Start at the bigger number and count up.

whyWrongByChoice.c: 8 is 4 + 4. That is one too many.

miniLesson.title: Basic Sums
bodyLines: Joining 4 items and 3 items gives 7 items.

conceptExplainer: You can make 10 first: 9 + 1 = 10, then add the remaining 6.

whyWrongByChoice.a: That spelling is missing the final e.
whyWrongByChoice.c: The letters u and a are swapped.

conceptExplainer: Some words have letter patterns we learn by practice.

miniLesson.title: Spelling Rule: Because
bodyLines: Remember: Big Elephants Can Always Understand Small Elephants (B-E-C-A-U-S-E).

whyCorrect: That is the dog! Dogs say woof.

whyWrongByChoice.a: That is a cow. Cows say moo.
whyWrongByChoice.c: That is a cat. Cats say meow.

conceptExplainer: Dogs are furry animal friends that bark woof!

miniLesson.title: Animal Sounds
bodyLines: Cats say meow, and cows say moo.

prompt: Can you tap the friendly lion?
whyCorrect: Roar! That is the brave lion.

whyWrongByChoice.a: That is a little rabbit with long ears.
whyWrongByChoice.c: That is a duck that swims and quacks.

conceptExplainer: Lions have big manes and love to roar.

miniLesson.title: The Lion
bodyLines: Lions are called the kings of the jungle.

prompt: How many apples do you see?
whyCorrect: Four apples! One, two, three, four.

whyWrongByChoice.a: Let's count together: 1, 2, 3, 4! That is 4, not 3.
whyWrongByChoice.c: Let's count together: 1, 2, 3, 4! That is 4, not 5.

conceptExplainer: Count each apple one time in order: 1, 2, 3, 4.

miniLesson.title: Counting One by One
bodyLines: Touch each item as you say its number: 1, 2, 3, 4!

prompt: How many stars are in the sky?
conceptExplainer: Three stars shine bright in the night.

prompt: Tap the same color! Find the red circle.
whyCorrect: Yes — that circle is bright red too!

whyWrongByChoice.a: That one is blue like the ocean. We wanted red.
whyWrongByChoice.c: That one is yellow like the sun. We wanted red.

conceptExplainer: Red is the color of strawberries and hearts.

miniLesson.title: Color Matching
bodyLines: Red matches red! Both circles share the same warm color.

prompt: Find the shape with 3 pointy corners!
whyCorrect: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 pointy corners.

whyWrongByChoice.a: Circles are round with no corners.

conceptExplainer: Tri means three! A triangle looks like a slice of pizza.

prompt: What is water called when it freezes?

whyWrongByChoice.a: Steam is water vapor when heated to boiling.
whyWrongByChoice.c: Clouds are tiny droplets condensed in the air.

conceptExplainer: Water exists in three states: solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (steam).

miniLesson.title: Three States of Matter
bodyLines: Water freezes into solid ice at 0°C (32°F).
When heated to 100°C (212°F), it evaporates into steam.

conceptExplainer: Multiplication is repeated addition: seven groups of six.
